title: Autonomous Acquisition of 4D-STEM Data to Dynamically-Sample Hidden Material Heterogeneities using Live Quantitative Analysis
content: Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) is a leading technique to characterize complex phenomena and features including orientation mapping [1], material phase distribution [2], local strain [3], potential [4], magnetism [5], and simultaneous imaging of light and heavy atoms [6]. However, as the desired field of view and resolution increases, 4D-STEM datasets can be extremely large and require an excessively long acquisition time. This creates an experimental challenge when studying heterogeneous features whose existence cannot easily be inferred and quantified from much faster techniques. Rather, these “hidden” features (e.g. orientation, phase analysis, polarization, charge density waves, etc.) are better visualized by directly considering the converged beam electron diffraction (CBED) patterns and quantifying the variation across the sample. While described as heterogeneous, these features may not vary over a short distance, creating further complications in deciding a minimum necessary sampling-rate to adequately describe the sample without oversampling, which wastes time and creates excessive damage in beam sensitive samples.
